tempo.basis: from four complete recordings, median 1:05 (Gerhaher or Tilling/Huber 1:02, Röschmann or Bostridge/Johnson 1:05, Fischer-Dieskau (DG) 1:05, Harteros 1:21), 1.5 s allowed for silence; Schumann marks it Munter, zart

phrases: When the evening breeze blows through the Piazzetta,
vɛn dʊrç diː piaˈtsɛta diː ˈaːbəntlʊft veːt
then you know, Ninetta, who stands waiting here.
dan vaɪst duː niˈnɛta veːr ˈvartənt hiːr ʃteːt
You know who recognises you despite veil and mask,
duː vaɪst veːr trɔts ˈʃlaɪər ʊnt ˈmaskə dɪç kɛnt
as Cupid knows Venus in the night sky.
viː ˈaːmɔr diː ˈveːnʊs am ˈnaxtfɪrmamɛnt
notes: Words by Ferdinand Freiligrath after Thomas Moore ("When through the Piazzetta"). IPA follows sung German (Bühnenaussprache): r rolled or flipped, final -er as [ər], ch after front vowels [ç]. Literal translation, for meaning.
